The flow is isentropic and quasi-one-dimensional with gamma equal to 1.4 and constant stagnation temperature.
Use the supersonic branch of the area-Mach relation A/A* = (1/M)((1 + 0.2 M^2)/1.2)^3.
Compute A1/A* for Mach 2.0 as 1.6875.
Compute A2/A* as 0.7 times A1/A*, giving 1.18125.
Solve the area-Mach relation on the supersonic branch to obtain the exit Mach number M2 equal to 1.507.
Compute the static temperature ratio T2/T1 as (1 + 0.2 M1^2)/(1 + 0.2 M2^2), which equals 1.2376.
Compute the exit-to-inlet velocity ratio V2/V1 as (M2/M1) times the square root of T2/T1, which equals 0.8385.
Express the increase in exit velocity compared to the inlet as V2/V1 minus 1, giving -0.1615 or -16.15 percent.
Report the result as a decrease in exit velocity of 16.15 percent relative to the inlet velocity.
